the ויש אומרים of the same baraita (barrier at the heart)

props.gloss_en: one sleeping in his garment who cannot put his head out for the cold makes a barrier with his garment at his neck and reads the Shema
some say: [he makes the barrier] at his heart
the tanna kama holds: the heart seeing the nakedness is permitted
one walking in filthy alleys places his hand over his mouth and reads the Shema
Rav Chisda's position: one walking in filthy alleys may not read the Shema (stated by his oath of refusal; named his by the Gemara at 24b.18)
Rav Huna: a Torah scholar may not stand in a place of filth
for he cannot stand without thinking of Torah
no difficulty: Rav Huna's prohibition speaks of one standing, his permission of one walking
one may think words of Torah everywhere except the bathhouse and the privy
here too: R' Yochanan's prohibition speaks of one standing, his permission of one walking
R' Abbahu was walking behind R' Yochanan reciting the Shema; when he reached the filthy alleys he fell silent, and asked: where shall I resume?
R' Yochanan: if you paused long enough to finish all of it, go back to the beginning
baraita: one walking in filthy alleys places his hand over his mouth and reads the Shema
baraita: one walking in filthy alleys may not read the Shema
moreover, if he was reading and came [there], he stops
R' Meyasha: of one who did not stop Scripture says 'I too gave them statutes that were not good, and laws by which they shall not live' (Ezek 20:25)
Rav Asi: [of him:] 'woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity' (Isa 5:18)
Rav Adda bar Ahava, from here: 'for he despised the word of the Lord' (Num 15:31)
R' Abbahu: of one who stopped Scripture says 'and through this matter you shall lengthen your days' (Deut 32:47)

objections.gloss_en: ותנא קמא הרי לבו רואה את הערוה! -- with the barrier at his neck, his heart sees his nakedness

objections.gloss_en: ומי אמר רב הונא הכי? והאמר רב הונא: תלמיד חכם אסור לו לעמוד במקום הטנופת, לפי שאי אפשר לו לעמוד בלי הרהור תורה -- if he may not even stand there, how may he read the Shema there?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: כאן בעומד, כאן במהלך (= p_okimta_huna_omed)

objections.gloss_en: ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי? והאמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן: בכל מקום מותר להרהר בדברי תורה חוץ מבית המרחץ ומבית הכסא -- if he may not even think Torah in a place of filth, how may he read the Shema there?

answered_by.gloss_en: וכי תימא: הכא נמי כאן בעומד כאן במהלך (= p_okimta_yochanan_omed) -- itself attacked by the R' Abbahu story (obj_ini_rabbi_abbahu) and defended at 24b.17

objections.gloss_en: איני? והא רבי אבהו הוה קא אזיל בתריה דרבי יוחנן... כי מטא במבואות המטונפות אישתיק... אמר ליה: אם שהית כדי לגמור את כולה חזור לראש -- R' Yochanan ruled on where to resume and did not tell him he should have kept reading while walking

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר ליה: לדידי לא סבירא לי, לדידך דסבירא לך, אם שהית כדי לגמור את כולה חזור לראש -- R' Yochanan answered on R' Abbahu's own view, not his
